title: response_format: actionable-strict-mode with granular error hints and OpenAI-compat mapping
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Introduce an 'actionable_strict' response_format mode: clearer schema error messages with JSONPath-based hints, token-offset suggestions for streamed responses, and OpenAI-compat error mapping. Backwards-compatible fallbacks enabled for streaming toolcalls.
description:
Motivation: Customers integrating structured outputs via response_format have reported opaque schema validation failures during streaming and tool/function calls (errors like 'invalid payload' with no actionable context). This PR introduces a new response_format mode 'actionable_strict' that keeps strict validation semantics while providing granular, developer-friendly diagnostics and a compatibility mapping layer for OpenAI-style clients.

What this PR does (summary): - Adds an 'actionable_strict' enforcement path in the response validator that emits structured error hints (schema path, expected/received types, approximate token-offset in the stream) instead of bare failures. - Implements a thin OpenAI-compat adapter that maps Redwood validation errors to familiar OpenAI error codes/messages so users migrating from OpenAI get predictable error shapes. - Improves streaming stability for structured outputs by snapshotting a stream checkpoint when a validation error is detected and exposing a small resume token that the console/SDKs can use to request a graceful rewind/retry. - Ensures tool/function calling behavior is safe under strict validation: tool-call boundaries are checkpointed and we will prefer a controlled fallback (emit 'tool_call_error' block) instead of aborting the entire stream. - Adds telemetry (schema.validation.latency_ms, schema.errors.count, schema.error_types.*) and unit + integration tests covering streaming resumes and OpenAI-compat responses.

Key design notes: - Error hints are intentionally non-sensitive: we do not include raw user data in error payloads; offsets are token-relative and bounded to a small window. - The OpenAI-compat mapping is opt-in via the 'openai_compat' request flag for backward compatibility; by default Redwood keeps native error shapes. - Fallback semantics: when streaming and strict validation fails, we try to emit a syntactic partial payload and a 'validation_note' event in the stream; SDKs are expected to surface this and offer a resume path.

Files changed (high level): - runtime/validator/response_validator.go: new actionable_strict path + mapping helpers - runtime/validator/stream_checkpoint.go: stream snapshot + resume token - api/adapters/openai/error_mapper.go: mapping table and tests - sdk/python/openai_compat.py: small helper for request flag - console/docs/response_format_actionable_strict.md: doc + examples - tests/integration/test_stream_resume.py: checks resume semantics - tests/unit/test_error_hints.py: tests for granular hints

Commits (summary): - Add actionable_strict enforcement and basic error hints - Wire stream checkpointing and resume token - OpenAI compatibility mapper and adapter flag - SDK helper and docs for actionable_strict - Tests and telemetry metrics - Address review feedback and cleanup

Why this is safe to merge: The change is additive and behind the new response_format mode and an explicit 'openai_compat' flag. Existing response_format modes (permissive/strict) are unchanged. Streaming fallback is conservative: we prefer to preserve client-visible partial payloads instead of silent aborts. Extensive unit and integration tests were added; CI green after fixing an initial threading race in stream_checkpoint.

Related work: builds on ENG-1142 (schema validation revamp) and ENG-1188 (stream resume primitives). Support ticket SUP-998 requested clearer error messages during streaming toolcalls.

How to try it: include "response_format": { "mode": "actionable_strict" } in the request body; to get OpenAI-shaped errors add "openai_compat": true. Example and SDK snippets documented in the added console doc.
commits: Add actionable_strict enforcement and error hints (Maya)
review_thread:
Liam O'Connor: Nice approach, can we keep the token-offset heuristic bounded to avoid leaking sensitive lengths?
Maya Singh: Agreed. I added a hard cap at 128 tokens in stream_checkpoint.go and a unit test.

Priya Nair: The OpenAI mapping should not accidentally change status codes for other adapters. Please ensure it's opt-in.
Maya Singh: It is opt-in; added explicit tests and a request-flag gating path in openai_compat.py.

Ethan Zhao: Integration test failed initially with race on stream checkpoint; is that fixed?
Maya Singh: Fixed by serializing checkpoint commits behind a small mutex, added retry + backoff in tests.

Priya Nair: Approving pending minor docs wording.
Priya Nair: Approved.
Liam O'Connor: LGTM, squash on merge.
